title.title: The Correspondence of the Yarnall family

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of the Yarnall family is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: I received thy letter which was very acceptable to me. Thee expresses thy weariness in respect to what passed when we were last together; but I would not have thee to be in the least concerned about it. For I do believe what thee said came from a sense of what ought to be, in respect to the plainess both in dress and furniture. And I have often remembered what thee said to me with much respect, that I would not have thee to be discouraged from bearing a testimony against wrong things when occasion presents. And it is my desire that thou mayest be enabled so to conduct in every respect. That it may appear that thee prefers true wisdom and virtue to every other confession, and I do hope that thee may become useful ation with propriety to thy own Friends’ satisfaction.
I take it kind that thee gave me some account of being in company with our Friend David Sands, whose expressions were comfortable and edifying to thee.

I have had an opportunity with Martha Dudley, and signified something of thy mind respecting what thee mentions in thy letter. And she expressed her unity with thy care, and seemed well satisfied about it.
We are in usual health at present, and should be glad to hear from our Friends and relations.

closer.salute: Now I conclude with my love to thee and remain thy well wishing Aunt
